title: Heavy Metal Pt I
summary: Part one of a two-part Stuff You Should Know episode on heavy metal. The hosts open with their personal metal listening histories and favorite bands, then debate what counts as metal versus hard rock (Led Zeppelin, Deep Purple, Rainbow, Van Halen). They trace Black Sabbath's origins, including Tony Iommi's fingertip injury and downtuning, and the Sabbath-versus-Judas Priest "first metal band" claim. They cover Iron Maiden and its mascot Eddie, the "heavy metal" phrase (William S. Burroughs, Lester Bangs), and the Birmingham and Detroit industrial roots. The episode then covers subgenres: hair metal, thrash (Big Four), death metal, black metal, industrial metal, new metal, groove metal, and the Grammys' metal categories. It ends with a teaser for part two.
topics: new wave of British heavy metal
origin of the phrase heavy metal
Stuff You Should Know metal two-parter

segments.title: Opening banter and hosts' metal backgrounds
segments.summary: The hosts joke about their metal fandom and the difficulty of covering the genre, then trade favorite bands and top-five lists.

segments.title: Favorite bands and listening histories
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck share their top metal bands, including Metallica, Black Sabbath, Iron Maiden, Helmet, Gojira, Godflesh and High on Fire, and discuss the MTV and radio influences of their youth.

segments.title: Defining metal
segments.summary: Chuck reads Britannica's definition of heavy metal, and the hosts agree the genre is fractured into many subgenres that are hard to define.

segments.title: Hard rock versus metal: Led Zeppelin, Deep Purple, Rainbow
segments.summary: The hosts debate whether Led Zeppelin, Deep Purple and Rainbow count as metal, noting Led Zeppelin's own denial, the Unholy Trinity of hard rock, and Lemmy's roadie past with Jimi Hendrix.

segments.title: Black Sabbath's origins and the first metal band claim
segments.summary: The hosts describe Black Sabbath's origins as Earth Blues Company from Birmingham, the name taken from a Boris Karloff film, and the claim that Judas Priest was formed the same year. They also discuss Ozzy Osbourne's solo career and the band's chart standing.

segments.title: Sabbath's early albums and Paranoid
segments.summary: The hosts say Sabbath's debut is bluesy but still metal, and that Paranoid is the metal album to beat, ranked number one by Rolling Stone.

segments.title: Tony Iommi's fingertip injury and downtuning
segments.summary: Chuck recounts Tony Iommi losing fingertips at a steel mill, and the hosts explain how he adapted with self-made prosthetics, lighter strings and downtuning, which shaped the band's sludgy sound.

segments.title: Sabbath's album art and mistakes
segments.summary: The hosts discuss Sabbath's imperfect studio takes and the iconic debut album cover, and how digital listening loses the physical album art experience.

segments.title: Iron Maiden and the mascot Eddie
segments.summary: The hosts cover Iron Maiden's 1975 origins with Paul Di'Anno, the band's influence, and their mascot Eddie, drawn by Derek Riggs, whose name came from the British 'h' dropping, and his appearances on album covers.

segments.title: Iron Maiden's songs and documentary
segments.summary: The hosts praise the varied themes of Iron Maiden's songs and mention a recent documentary Chuck plans to watch.
topics: The Loneliness of the Long Distance Runner

segments.title: Iron Maiden's popularity and poll claims
segments.summary: Josh says Number of the Beast was voted the best British record of the last sixty years in a 2012 poll, and that Iron Maiden has sold about 130 million albums. Chuck questions the poll's methodology.

segments.title: Judas Priest, Motorhead, and Van Halen debate
segments.summary: The hosts compare Judas Priest and Iron Maiden, Josh adds Motorhead to his list, and they debate whether Van Halen and other classic rock acts are metal, with Chuck saying no and Josh saying yes.

segments.title: Origin of the phrase heavy metal
segments.summary: The hosts trace the phrase heavy metal, noting Steppenwolf's 'Born to Be Wild' lyric about cars, William S. Burroughs' 'Uranium Willy' and 'heavy metal' drug, and Lester Bangs' 1970 review. Dina Weinstein is cited for the Birmingham and Detroit industrial roots of the genre.

segments.title: Industrial cities and metal's audience
segments.summary: The hosts discuss Weinstein's argument that polluted, working-class Birmingham and Detroit gave metal its sensibility and fan base.

segments.title: Subgenres, New Wave of British Heavy Metal, and touring
segments.summary: Josh describes the British new wave of heavy metal, the lack of radio support that led bands to tour heavily, and the stage shows of the 1980s. Chuck covers 1980s hair metal bands and King Diamond and Mercyful Fate's dark metal and corpse paint.
topics: new wave of British heavy metal

segments.title: Death metal origins
segments.summary: Josh names Possessed's 1985 album Seven Churches as a death metal starting point and describes death metal's growled vocals. Chuck explains that such bands were underground and rarely on radio or MTV. Morbid Angel, Autopsy and Cannibal Corpse are named.

segments.title: Industrial metal: Ministry and Godflesh
segments.summary: The hosts discuss Ministry's 1986 album Twitch as a bridge to industrial music, and Godflesh's slow, drum-machine-driven industrial metal from Birmingham.

segments.title: Birmingham as a metal hub
segments.summary: The hosts note Birmingham's central role in metal, with Godflesh and other bands coming from the city.

segments.title: Grammy metal awards, grunge, and new metal
segments.summary: Chuck describes the Grammy metal category, including Jethro Tull's 1989 win over Metallica's ...And Justice for All. Josh explains that grunge pushed metal out of the spotlight, and new metal, alt metal, and progressive metal such as Tool, System of a Down and Dream Theater followed.

segments.title: Pantera and groove metal
segments.summary: Josh describes Pantera's start as a glam rock band and their role in groove metal, and Chuck agrees.

segments.title: Thrash bands: Metallica, Megadeth, Slayer
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the Big Four of thrash, Chuck's experiences with Metallica, Dave Mustaine's split from Metallica and founding of Megadeth, and Josh's views on Slayer and Megadeth.

segments.title: Black metal origins
segments.summary: Josh explains black metal's high-pitched screamed vocals and its satanic image. He names Venom, Bathory and Mayhem as early or key bands, and says Mayhem was tied to real violence.

segments.title: Mayhem's Dawn of the Black Hearts and the Norwegian scene
segments.summary: Chuck describes the Dawn of the Black Hearts bootleg cover, a photograph of Mayhem's singer after his suicide, taken by bandmate Euronymous. Josh adds that the scene includes white supremacists, mentions Emperor, and says he finds the sound off-putting.

segments.title: Part one wrap-up and teaser
segments.summary: The hosts say this is part one of a two-part metal episode, with a short stuff episode to follow, and close the show.
